questions.question_text: At a mountain resort, the probability of snow on any day is $0.4$. When it snows ($S$), the cable car operates ($C$) $50\%$ of the time. When it does not snow ($S'$), the cable car operates $90\%$ of the time. Given that the cable car is operating on a randomly chosen day, find the probability that it is snowing, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Used the forward conditional probability $P(C \mid S) = 0.5$ instead of the reverse conditional probability.
Calculated the probability that it was not snowing given the cable car is operating ($P(S' \mid C)$).
Stated the joint probability $P(S \cap C) = 0.20$ without dividing by $P(C)$.

questions.question_text: A factory produces microchips on two lines: Line 1 produces $80\%$ of all chips and has a $3\%$ defect rate; Line 2 produces $20\%$ of all chips and has a $7\%$ defect rate. A microchip is selected at random and found to be defective. Find the probability that it came from Line 1, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Used the production proportion $P(L_1) = 0.8$ without weighting by the defect rate.
Calculated the probability that the defective chip came from Line 2.
Compared the two defect rates $\frac{3}{3+7}$ ignoring the differing line production volumes.

questions.question_text: A clinic tests for an allergy that affects $20\%$ of patients ($A$). The test gives a positive result ($+$) for $90\%$ of allergic patients and for $10\%$ of non-allergic patients ($A'$). Given that a patient tests positive, find the probability that they are allergic, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Divided the wrong branch by $P(+)$, finding $P(A' \mid +) = \frac{0.08}{0.26}$, the probability the patient is not allergic.
Left the false-positive branch unweighted, taking $P(+) = 0.18 + 0.10 = 0.28$ instead of multiplying $0.10$ by $P(A') = 0.80$.
Left the false-positive branch unweighted ($P(+) = 0.28$) and then divided the non-allergic branch $0.10$ by it.

questions.question_text: Jar A contains $5$ green and $1$ red marble. Jar B contains $2$ green and $4$ red marbles. A fair coin is tossed to select a jar ($P(A) = P(B) = \frac{1}{2}$), and one marble is drawn. Given that the drawn marble is red, find the probability that Jar B was chosen, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Calculated the probability that Jar A was chosen given a red marble.
Used the proportion of red marbles in Jar B alone ($\frac{4}{6}$) without conditioning.
Found the joint probability $P(B \cap R) = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}$ without dividing by $P(R)$.

questions.question_text: In a driving school, $60\%$ of students complete a preparatory course ($C$). Of those who complete it, $85\%$ pass the test on their first attempt ($P$). Of those who do not complete it ($C'$), only $50\%$ pass on their first attempt. Given that a student passed on their first attempt, find the probability that they completed the preparatory course, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Divided the wrong branch by $P(P)$, finding $P(C' \mid P) = \frac{0.20}{0.71}$, the probability the student did not complete the course.
Swapped the two group proportions, using $P(C) = 0.40$ and $P(C') = 0.60$, giving $\frac{0.34}{0.64}$.
Swapped the two group proportions ($P(C) = 0.40$, $P(C') = 0.60$) and then divided the non-completer branch $0.30$ by the total $0.64$.

questions.question_text: A manufacturer sources $45\%$ of components from Supplier A and $55\%$ from Supplier B. Components from Supplier A have a $4\%$ failure rate, while components from Supplier B have an $8\%$ failure rate. A randomly chosen component failed. Find the probability that it was supplied by Supplier A, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Divided the wrong branch by $P(F)$, finding $\frac{0.044}{0.062}$, the probability the failed component came from Supplier B.
Attached the failure rates to the wrong suppliers, using $8\%$ for A and $4\%$ for B, giving $\frac{0.036}{0.058}$.
Attached the failure rates to the wrong suppliers ($8\%$ for A, $4\%$ for B) and then divided the Supplier B branch $0.022$ by the total $0.058$.

questions.question_text: A blood test for a condition with a $10\%$ prevalence has a $92\%$ sensitivity ($P(+ \mid D) = 0.92$) and an $8\%$ false positive rate ($P(+ \mid D') = 0.08$). Given that a person tests negative ($-$), find the probability that they are disease-free ($D'$), as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Calculated the probability that the person has the disease despite testing negative.
Quoted the test specificity $P(- \mid D') = 0.92$ instead of finding $P(D' \mid -)$.
Used the prior probability of being healthy $P(D') = 0.90$ without updating.

questions.question_text: A box contains $2$ fair coins and $1$ two-headed coin. One coin is randomly chosen ($P = \frac{2}{3}$ for fair, $P = \frac{1}{3}$ for two-headed) and tossed. It lands on Heads. Find the probability that the chosen coin is the two-headed coin, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Used the prior probability of choosing the two-headed coin without updating.
Assumed seeing a Head guarantees the coin is two-headed.
Calculated the probability of choosing a fair coin instead of the two-headed coin.

questions.question_text: On days when it rains ($30\%$ of days), bus traffic has a $40\%$ chance of significant delays ($D$). On dry days, bus traffic has a $10\%$ chance of significant delays. Given that a bus trip experienced significant delays, find the probability that it was a dry day, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Divided the wrong branch by $P(D)$, finding $\frac{0.12}{0.19}$, the probability that it was raining given the delays.
Read the $30\%$ as the proportion of dry days, so used $P(\text{Dry}) = 0.30$ and $P(\text{Rain}) = 0.70$, giving $\frac{0.03}{0.31}$.
Read the $30\%$ as the proportion of dry days ($P(\text{Rain}) = 0.70$) and then divided the rainy branch $0.28$ by the total $0.31$.

questions.question_text: A screening program tests for a rare genetic mutation present in $2$ in $1000$ individuals ($p = 0.002$). The test has a $100\%$ true positive rate ($P(+ \mid M) = 1$) and a $5\%$ false positive rate ($P(+ \mid M') = 0.05$). Find the probability that an individual has the mutation given that they tested positive, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Calculated the probability that the individual does not have the mutation given a positive test.
Assumed a 100% true positive rate means a positive test is 100% certain to indicate the mutation.
Approximated $0.998 \approx 1.0$ giving $\frac{0.002}{0.052} = \frac{1}{26}$ instead of using exact values.
